Clinical Diagnosis & History: T1 adenocarcinoma of the sigmoid colon, biopsy proven, for laparoscopic low anterior resection with regional lymphadenectomy, possible ostomy. SIGMOID COLON, SEGMENTAL RESECTION: - INVASIVE MODERATELY DIFFERENTIATED ADENOCARCINOMA, CONVENTIONAL TYPE, MEASURING 1.6 CM IN GREATEST DIMENSION. - TUMOR INVADES SUBMUCOSA ONLY. - NO LYMPHOVASCULAR INVASION IDENTIFIED. - ALL SURGICAL MARGINS ARE NEGATIVE FOR CARCINOMA. - FOUR OF FOURTEEN REGIONAL LYMPH NODES ARE POSITIVE FOR METASTATIC ADENOCARCINOMA (4/14). - NO EXTRANODAL EXTENSION IS IDENTIFIED. - APPENDICEAL SEROSA AND DISTAL RESECTION MARGIN ARE UNINVOLVED. - PATHOLOGIC STAGE: pT1 pN2a pM0. 2). The specimen is received fresh, labeled, "sigmoid colon and rectum with attached mesentery and lymph nodes". It consists of a segment of large bowel measuring 18.4 cm in length with attached mesenteric fat measuring 9.0 x 7.5 x 2.5 cm. A firm ulcerated lesion is identified 6.0 cm from the distal margin and 9.5 cm from the proximal margin, measuring 1.6 x 1.4 x 0.5 cm. The lesion is entirely submitted for histology. The surrounding mucosa shows mild diverticular change. The mesentery yields fourteen lymph nodes ranging from 0.2 cm to 1.1 cm, entirely submitted. The specimen is inked as follows: proximal-blue, distal-red, radial-black. Summary of Sections: A1-A2 proximal margin, A3-A4 distal margin, A5-A8 tumor, A9-A10 uninvolved bowel, A11-A18 lymph nodes. 2). The specimen is received fresh, labeled, "anastomotic donuts". It consists of two mucosal ring fragments measuring 1.1 cm and 1.3 cm, grossly unremarkable. Tumor extends through the muscularis mucosae into the submucosa without penetration of the muscularis propria. The positive lymph nodes show metastatic carcinoma with focal capsular distortion but no definite extranodal spread. Special Studies: MMR immunohistochemistry is intact for MLH1, PMS2, MSH2 and MSH6. Comment: Findings are consistent with a resected early invasive colorectal adenocarcinoma with regional nodal metastases. Clinical correlation and consideration of adjuvant therapy are recommended. SPECIMEN. A. Left hemicolectomy. B. Pericolonic lymph nodes. CLINICAL NOTES. PRE-OP DIAGNOSIS: Colon cancer. GROSS DESCRIPTION. A. Received fresh, subsequently fixed in formalin, labeled "left hemicolectomy" is a 24.5 cm segment of colon with attached pericolonic adipose tissue measuring up to 7.2 cm in thickness. The serosa is smooth and tan-pink with focal fibrous adhesions. On opening, there is an ulcerated, infiltrative tan-white mass in the descending colon measuring 3.8 x 3.1 x 0.9 cm. The lesion is centered 12.4 cm from the proximal margin and 8.6 cm from the distal margin. The mass extends through the muscularis propria into the pericolonic soft tissue but does not grossly involve the serosal surface. The remainder of the mucosa is unremarkable without additional mass lesion. Multiple pericolonic lymph node candidates are identified in the attached fat, the largest measuring 1.1 cm in greatest dimension. Representative sections are submitted in 14 cassettes as labeled. BLOCK SUMMARY: 1-2 proximal and distal margins; 3-6 tumor with deepest invasion; 7-8 tumor to serosa; 9-11 uninvolved colon; 12-14 lymph nodes. B. Received fresh, subsequently fixed in formalin, labeled "pericolonic lymph nodes" are multiple irregular tan-black soft tissue fragments with an aggregate measurement of 2.0 x 1.3 x 0.5 cm. The specimens are entirely submitted in two cassettes. MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION. A, B. Microscopic examination performed and summarized below: Histologic type: Adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated. Histologic grade: Grade 2. Primary tumor (pT): Tumor invades through muscularis propria into pericolonic tissue, greatest dimension 3.8 cm (pT2). Margins of resection: Negative for carcinoma; all margins free of tumor. Lymphovascular invasion: Present. Perineural invasion: Present. Tumor budding: Low. Regional lymph nodes (pN): Metastatic adenocarcinoma is identified in 2 of 7 regional lymph nodes examined, with largest metastatic deposit measuring 4 mm; no extranodal extension identified (pN1). Distant metastasis (pM): No evidence of distant metastasis identified in the material examined (pM0). Additional findings: Background diverticulosis and focal chronic active colitis adjacent to tumor. DIAGNOSIS. A. Colon, left hemicolectomy: Moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, 3.8 cm, invading into pericolonic soft tissue, margins negative, lymphovascular and perineural invasion present. Metastatic carcinoma in 2 of 7 lymph nodes (pT2 pN1 pM0). B. Pericolonic lymph nodes, biopsy: Metastatic adenocarcinoma in 0 of 2 fragments with nodal tissue not identified in one fragment; see part A for nodal staging. End of report.

Diagnosis / Diagnoses: Left upper lobectomy specimen with a peripheral invasive pulmonary adenocarcinoma, acinar predominant with focal lepidic growth, moderately differentiated (G2), measuring 3.8 cm in greatest dimension. Tumor is confined to the lung parenchyma without pleural penetration or invasion of the chest wall. Bronchial, vascular, and parenchymal margins are free of tumor. Lymphovascular invasion is present. Hilar and mediastinal lymph node dissection performed; two of fourteen lymph nodes show metastatic carcinoma, with deposits confined to the nodes and no extranodal extension. Remaining nodes show only reactive hyperplasia. No evidence of distant metastasis identified on preoperative imaging or in the sampled material. Tumor stage thus: pT2 pN1 (2/14), pM0; G2. Clinical correlation recommended.

DIAGNOSIS. (A) RIGHT BREAST, MODIFIED RADICAL MASTECTOMY: INVASIVE DUCTAL CARCINOMA, NO SPECIAL TYPE, HIGH GRADE (NOTTINGHAM HISTOLOGIC GRADE 3). Tumor measures 6.4 cm in greatest dimension. Tumor extends into adjacent fibroadipose breast tissue but does not involve skin or chest wall. Extensive ductal carcinoma in situ, high nuclear grade, solid and comedo types, present in association with invasive carcinoma. Lymphovascular invasion identified. Nipple and areola, no tumor present. Surgical margins of resection free of tumor; closest margin is posterior, 1.1 cm from invasive carcinoma. (B) RIGHT AXILLARY LYMPH NODES: Seven of fifteen lymph nodes positive for metastatic carcinoma, with largest metastatic focus 1.6 cm. Focal extranodal extension present. PATHOLOGIC STAGE: pT3 pN2 cM0. COMMENT. The invasive carcinoma forms irregular nests, cords and poorly formed glands within a desmoplastic stroma. By imaging workup and clinical evaluation, there is no evidence of distant metastatic disease. Estrogen receptor positive, progesterone receptor low positive, HER2 negative by in situ hybridization. GROSS DESCRIPTION. (A) RIGHT BREAST, MODIFIED RADICAL MASTECTOMY - A mastectomy specimen with attached ellipse of skin and nipple-areolar complex, overall measuring 22.5 X 18.0 X 6.5 cm. The skin ellipse measures 14.0 X 5.5 cm and the nipple measures 1.2 X 1.0 X 0.8 cm. On sectioning, there is an ill-defined firm gray-white stellate mass in the upper outer and central breast measuring 6.4 X 5.8 X 4.9 cm. The mass is 1.1 cm from the posterior margin, 2.4 cm from the anterior soft tissue margin, 3.2 cm from the nearest skin margin, and 4.0 cm from the nipple base. Surrounding the invasive lesion are areas of tan-white granular tissue consistent with associated in situ carcinoma spanning up to 7.3 cm. The remaining breast parenchyma is fibrofatty with focal dense stromal fibrosis. SECTION CODE: A1, nipple and retroareolar tissue; A2-A4, tumor to posterior margin; A5-A6, tumor to anterior margin; A7, tumor to skin; A8-A12, representative sections of invasive tumor; A13-A15, sections of tumor with adjacent DCIS; A16, uninvolved breast tissue. (B) RIGHT AXILLARY LYMPH NODES - An aggregate of fibroadipose tissue measuring 11.0 X 8.0 X 2.5 cm. Fifteen lymph nodes are identified, ranging from 0.4 X 0.3 X 0.2 cm to 2.3 X 1.5 X 1.2 cm. Seven lymph nodes show metastatic carcinoma, including one node with extranodal extension. SECTION CODE: B1, four possible lymph nodes; B2, three lymph nodes; B3, two lymph nodes, one bisected; B4, two lymph nodes; B5, one lymph node, bisected; B6, one lymph node, bisected; B7, two lymph nodes. CLINICAL HISTORY. Palpable right breast mass, abnormal axillary nodes on ultrasound. CT chest/abdomen/pelvis and bone scan negative for distant metastasis. SNOMED CODES. 4, 7.

PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS: LEFT LUNG, UPPER LOBE, WEDGE RESECTION: INVASIVE ADENOCARCINOMA, acinar predominant, moderately differentiated (grade 2), measuring 3.4 cm in greatest dimension. Tumor invades through visceral pleura but not chest wall. No lymphovascular invasion is identified. Stapled parenchymal margin is negative for tumor, 1.1 cm from the closest inked margin. LEVEL 5 AND LEVEL 10 LYMPH NODES, EXCISION: Four lymph nodes examined, all negative for metastatic carcinoma (0:4). AJCC 8th Edition pathologic stage: pT2a pN0 pM0. Tumor is confined to the resected lobe; no satellite nodules are identified. Immunohistochemistry shows TTF-1 and Napsin A positivity, consistent with pulmonary primary. CLINICAL DATA: History of persistent cough and hemoptysis. CT chest demonstrated a spiculated left upper lobe mass. Operation: Video-assisted thoracoscopic wedge resection with mediastinal lymph node sampling. Operative Findings: No pleural implants or distant disease identified. TISSUE SUBMITTED: A/1. Left upper lobe mass. B/2. Level 5 lymph node. C/3. Level 10 lymph node. GROSS DESCRIPTION: The specimen is received fresh in three parts labeled with the patient?s name and accession number. Part A consists of a wedge resection of lung measuring 8.2 x 4.5 x 2.1 cm with an ill-defined tan-white firm mass (3.4 x 2.9 x 2.6 cm) located 0.8 cm from the pleural surface and 1.1 cm from the staple line. The pleural surface is intact and glistening. The remaining parenchyma shows mild emphysematous change. Part B consists of two anthracotic lymph nodes measuring 0.7 cm and 0.4 cm. Part C consists of two lymph nodes measuring 0.6 cm and 0.3 cm. All nodes are entirely submitted. MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION: Sections show an infiltrative gland-forming neoplasm with desmoplastic stroma and focal lepidic growth. Tumor cells have enlarged hyperchromatic nuclei, moderate eosinophilic cytoplasm, and occasional mitotic figures. No definite lymphatic or vascular permeation is seen. The visceral pleura is focally involved by tumor. All lymph nodes are free of metastatic carcinoma on H&E and cytokeratin stain. COMMENT: Findings support primary pulmonary adenocarcinoma, completely excised. Correlation with imaging shows no evidence of distant metastasis. Selected slides of this case were reviewed by Dr. Service, who concurs.
